diagnoses.description:
The agent failed to carry forward its own validation that the ~1.398 d peak was a half-period alias and instead selected the highest BLS peak (which can prefer the half-period when primary/secondary or odd/even effects exist) without reapplying the odd/even consistency criterion at the final selection step.
Evidence: Turn 13: the agent’s own BLS odd/even test favored ~2P: "at ~2P=2.79879348 d ... odd-even fraction ~-0.00384 (consistent odd/even depths), favoring the ~2.799 d interpretation as the true orbital period." Yet Turn 16 refined and Turn 17/18 reported and wrote "1.39825" as the final orbital period.
Trajectory location: turns 13 vs 16-18

Narrow refinement around the strongest peak can lock in an alias if the global optimum corresponds to a harmonic; a robust approach would also test 2P (and possibly P/2) with consistency checks (odd/even, secondary eclipse, transit shape) before finalizing.
Evidence: The refinement explicitly optimized only around the single best coarse BLS peak: "coarse best (likelihood) 1.3982309087784257" then refined within +/-0.2% of that value, never evaluating the corresponding doubled period (~2.7965–2.7988 d) under the same objective.
Trajectory location: turn 16

location_policy: native trajectory locations retained in description; no inferred Skill location
